title: The magazine blurb about piloting his own plane
summary: Goines reads a wartime blurb; Hawkins denies piloting or a South America tour.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I wanted to read this to you. It's that blurb that has you piloting your family around in your own plane. You know?
Oh, Yeah? I'd like to hear it. Yeah.

It says: 'One of the most versatile maestros, Erskine Hawkins, plays every instrument in the band. Whenever a musician is absent because of illness, Hawkins sits in his place and leads the group from there. 'Born in Birmingham, Alabama, Hawkins began study of the trumpet at Alabama State Teachers' College. It was while instructing at the college that he created his first

band with the students of the class. "Dubbed the "20th Century Gabriel" because of his unique musical style, Erskine specializes in the high register, and is one of the exclusive C above high C contingent. He relaxes by piloting his family in his own plane, and plans to make a good will airplane tour of South America after the war. [Hawkins Lyrics] "All in all, our neighbors to the south are in for a treat." So, you didn't do that, I guess?
Not the plane. Not the piloting. No.
Did you, did you, well, you didn't go on the good will airplane tour of South America, but did you go on a tour of South America after the war?
No. Cause you looked so surprised when I mentioned it.
Right. Very much. I was looking forward to that. Maybe they misunderstood me. That's good.
